= {project_name}

image:https://github.com/gesinn-it/Matomo/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg[CI,link=https://github.com/gesinn-it/Matomo/actions/workflows/ci.yml]
image:https://codecov.io/gh/gesinn-it/Matomo/graph/badge.svg[Coverage,link=https://codecov.io/gh/gesinn-it/Matomo]

Matomo is a MediaWiki extension that adds privacy-friendly Matomo pageview
tracking. It tracks only which pages are viewed, how often, and in what
sequence — no personally identifiable information is collected.

== Documentation

For Matomo itself see https://matomo.org[matomo.org].

== Configuration

Set these variables in `LocalSettings.php` after loading the extension.

[cols="1,1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Variable |Default |Description

|`$wgMatomoURL`
|`""`
|Hostname (and optional path) of the Matomo instance to send pageview data to, e.g. `matomo.example.org`. Tracking is disabled while this is empty.

|`$wgMatomoIDSite`
|`""`
|The numeric Matomo site ID to record pageviews under. Tracking is disabled while this is empty.

|`$wgMatomoProtocol`
|`"auto"`
|Protocol used to load the Matomo tracker script: `"auto"` (mirrors the current page's protocol), `"http"`, or `"https"`.

|`$wgMatomoIgnoreGroups`
|`[ "bot", "sysop" ]`
|User groups excluded from pageview tracking. A user is excluded if they belong to at least one listed group. Set to `[]` to track all users.

|`$wgMatomoCustomJS`
|`[]`
|A list of extra `_paq` commands to push after the core tracking commands, e.g. `[ [ "setDocumentTitle", "custom title" ], [ "trackEvent", "category", "action" ] ]`. Lets administrators extend tracking (custom variables, events, etc.) without patching the extension.

|`$wgMatomoDisableCookies`
|`true`
|Whether to push Matomo's `disableCookies` command before the core tracking commands, so tracking sets no first-party cookies regardless of the Matomo server configuration. Set to `false` to allow cookie-based tracking.
|===

Local testing and CI are supported by Docker and Make:

== Versioning and Releases

'''

*Versioning Convention — Semantic Versioning*

This project follows https://semver.org/[Semantic Versioning].

Version numbers follow the format:

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`

Version increment rules:

* MAJOR — incompatible or breaking changes
* MINOR — backwards-compatible feature additions
* PATCH — backwards-compatible bug fixes

Breaking changes include (but are not limited to):

* incompatible API changes
* removal or renaming of public interfaces
* behavior changes that may break existing integrations
* increased minimum runtime or dependency requirements
* incompatible configuration or data format changes
* dependency upgrades that introduce breaking changes for users

Breaking changes must always increment the MAJOR version.
